intervals.quote: In preparation for data taking during run 3 of the LHC, the MoEDAL detector has been upgraded to MoEDAL-MAPP. The addition detector, MAPP (MoEDAL Apparatus for Penetrating Particles), was approved in 2021

end.note: CERN schedule: the LHC resumes operation in mid-2030; the rest of the CERN complex restarts in stages from mid-2028.

intervals.label: Long Shutdown 3
intervals.locator: home.cern/science/long-shutdown-3, item of 5 August 2026 "The LHC is being warmed up from near absolute zero to room temperature"
intervals.note: MoEDAL searches for particles produced in LHC collisions, so it is idle while the LHC is shut down; this is an inference, since no MoEDAL-specific statement about this shutdown was found. Status is shutdown, not upgrade. The collaboration's home page (checked 2026-10-25) does not mention LS3 or an upgrade. No source consulted says that upgrade work on MoEDAL is under way in LS3. A 2022-23 paper describes MAPP-2, a planned second phase of the MAPP detector, as 'planned for installation during the long shutdown (LS3) prior to the startup of HL-LHC' (J. Pinfold, arXiv:2209.03988 v2); no 2026 source consulted confirms that installation has begun. Start and end are the LHC-wide Long Shutdown 3 dates. CERN's 5 August 2026 item says 'The cryogenics team has been running the warm-up sequence since LS3 began on 29 June 2026' and that the stored helium is kept 'ready to be used again once the accelerator resumes operation in mid-2030'; CERN's 29 June 2026 article says 'The HiLumi LHC, scheduled to begin operation in 2030'. The end is a schedule value, not a reported event.
intervals.quote: Following its final physics run, the accelerator has been switched off to begin CERN’s Long Shutdown 3 (LS3) ... The HiLumi LHC, scheduled to begin operation in 2030

physics_goals.quote: It is dedicated to the search for highly ionizing particle avatars of physics beyond the Standard Model, extending significantly the discovery horizon of the LHC.
physics_goals.value: Search for magnetic monopoles and other highly-ionizing avatars of physics beyond the Standard Model (dyons, Q-balls, black-hole remnants, multiply/massively charged particles)

physics_goals.quote: to extend MoEDAL’s physics reach by providing sensitivity to milli-charged particles and long-lived exotic particles
physics_goals.value: Extend sensitivity, via the MAPP upgrade, to milli-charged and long-lived exotic particles

summary.plain: MoEDAL is an unusual CERN experiment that mostly just sits there: sheets of plastic and jars of special metal quietly record the trails of exotic, heavily-charged particles -- like magnetic monopoles -- that might be created in LHC collisions at the LHCb cavern.
summary.technical: Passive, non-electronic detector at LHC Point 8 (co-located with LHCb): 125 Nuclear Track Detector stacks (47 m² deployed plastic) plus ~1 t of paramagnetic trapping detectors and TimePix monitoring, searching for magnetic monopoles and other highly-ionizing BSM particles. Proposed February 1998, approved as the LHC's seventh experiment in December 2009; the MAPP extension was approved in 2021.

unique_capabilities.quote: The main passive elements of the MoEDAL detector do not require a trigger system, electronic readout, or online computerized data acquisition.
unique_capabilities.value: An unconventional, largely passive detector (no trigger, electronic readout or online DAQ for its main elements) using Nuclear Track Detector stacks and paramagnetic trapping volumes rather than a conventional electronic detector
